provenance.note: Seed layer for /visakhapatnam/shoreline: OSM coastline geometry, seaward face only (most seaward vertex per 200 m bin along the 50 degree coast axis; the Visakhapatnam Port inner harbour and the Gangavaram port are chorded across), carrying the official stretch classes. NCCR's national assessment (Kankara et al. 2018, Table 16) covers the undivided district (136.98 km, 1990-2016). The MoES reply to Lok Sabha USQ 2638 (11 Dec 2024) covers the present district (68.08 km) and classes Yarada, RK Beach, Mangamari Peta to Bheemili and Bheemunipatnam to Pedanagamayyapalem as Low Erosion. The two district figures describe different boundaries and are not compared. Each zone's period is the analysis window of its record: 1990-2016 for the zones resting on NCCR's Table 16 (I, III, V, VI). USQ 2638 states no window, so the 1990-2018 on the four MoES-classed zones (II, IV, VII, VIII) is our inference: it is the window MoES gives for the same updated NCCR atlas of 25 March 2022 (PIB release, 31 Mar 2022; Rajya Sabha USQ 498, 21 Jul 2022). mean_erosion_m_yr is null by design: we have found no public source that gives per-zone rates; rates come from the computed transect layer. transect_masks tell the GEE stage which transects to drop (harbour chords) or mark low confidence (breakwaters, piers, the Gangavaram port's built flanks, the Dolphin's Nose headland, river mouths, and two transects, at RK Beach and north of the Gosthani mouth, whose measured waterline jumps 180 m or more between epochs up to 2015). Geometry is fetched live from Overpass, hence internal_inputs [].

properties.summary: The southern beaches from Appikonda up to the Gangavaram port. NCCR's shoreline assessment covers the whole district coast, but this stretch is not among the erosion-prone ones the Ministry of Earth Sciences named in December 2024, and we have not found a published rate for it. Our transects give the only per-point rates here that we know of. Transects on the shore the port built beside its breakwaters, and beside a small river mouth just south of it, are marked low confidence.
properties.source_label: NCCR National Assessment of Shoreline Changes 1990-2016 (Kankara et al. 2018)

properties.summary: From the Gangavaram port north past Yarada beach to the Dolphin's Nose headland. Yarada is one of four Visakhapatnam stretches classed Low Erosion in the Ministry of Earth Sciences' reply in the Lok Sabha on 11 December 2024 (NCCR's assessment; Low Erosion means the shore moves back 0.5 to 3 m a year). The ministry gives no extent for Yarada, so we do not extend the class to the port flanks or the headland. NCCR's 2018 report credits the Kailasa and Yarada ranges with keeping Visakhapatnam district's coast the most stable in Andhra Pradesh; the Yarada hills rise behind this zone. The port basin has no beach to measure, so its transects are left out; those beside its breakwaters and at the headland are marked low confidence.
properties.source_label: MoES reply to Lok Sabha USQ 2638 (11 Dec 2024), from NCCR's shoreline assessment

properties.zone_name: Visakhapatnam Port entrance and inner harbour
properties.summary: Dolphin's Nose to the Naval Coastal Battery: the Visakhapatnam Port entrance and inner harbour. A harbour basin has no beach to measure, so the baseline is drawn straight across it and no transects are kept here. The port moves sand that builds up south of its south breakwater to the beach north of its north breakwater (sand bypassing, CWC/NIO coastal erosion guidelines 2020).

properties.zone_name: RK Beach: Coastal Battery - Kursura - Pedda Waltair
properties.summary: The city beach, classed Low Erosion in the Ministry of Earth Sciences' 2024 reply. RK Beach is a managed beach: the port moves sand from south of its harbour onto this shore (sand bypassing, CWC/NIO 2020), and a Rs 20 crore sand-trap dredging for beach nourishment was inaugurated on 12 February 2023 (VPA Administration Report 2022-23). A stable or advancing waterline here reflects that added sand, not only natural change.
properties.source_label: MoES reply to Lok Sabha USQ 2638 (11 Dec 2024), from NCCR's shoreline assessment

properties.zone_name: Lawson's Bay - Tenneti - Jodugullapalem - Sagar Nagar
properties.summary: The shore below the Kailasagiri hills: Lawson's Bay, Tenneti Park, Jodugullapalem and Sagar Nagar. NCCR's shoreline assessment covers the whole district coast, but this stretch is not among the erosion-prone ones the Ministry of Earth Sciences named in December 2024, and we have not found a published rate for it. Our transects give the only per-point rates here that we know of.
properties.source_label: NCCR National Assessment of Shoreline Changes 1990-2016 (Kankara et al. 2018)
